dialogue.text: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.
dialogue.zh: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロのダビデの物語は、少年王が命を奪った話ではありません。
dialogue.local: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.
dialogue.en: The story of Michelangelo's David is anything but the story of a teenage boy king who slew the life.

dialogue.text: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,
dialogue.zh: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,
dialogue.ja: 彼の詩の一つで、ミケランジェロはこう書いています、
dialogue.local: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,
dialogue.en: In one of his poems, Michelangelo wrote,

dialogue.text: "'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'"
dialogue.zh: "'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'"
dialogue.ja: 「Somedi ese de Broutdo、私は醜いと知っている。」
dialogue.local: "'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'"
dialogue.en: "'Somedi ese de Broutdo, I know I am ugly.'"

dialogue.text: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.
dialogue.zh: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.
dialogue.ja: 彼の鼻は折れて顔に押しつぶされたように見え、彼はそれが乞食のように見せていると言いました。
dialogue.local: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.
dialogue.en: His nose was broken and appeared crushed into his face, which he said gave him the look of a beggar.

dialogue.text: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.
dialogue.zh: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.
dialogue.ja: 彼は自分の容姿に苦しみ、自分の体から孤立していました。
dialogue.local: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.
dialogue.en: He was tortured by his appearance and alienated from his own body.

dialogue.text: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.
dialogue.zh: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.
dialogue.ja: それにもかかわらず、あるいはそのために、彼は崇高な完璧さを追求して生涯を費やしました。
dialogue.local: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.
dialogue.en: Despite or perhaps because of this, he would spend his life in pursuit of sublime perfection.

dialogue.text: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.
dialogue.zh: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.
dialogue.ja: 彼は自分の容姿を変えることはほとんどできませんでしたが、自分のダビデ像が男性美の基準になるようにしました。
dialogue.local: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.
dialogue.en: He could do little about his own looks, but he would make sure his David would be the standard by which male beauty would be judged.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロは自分が神の道具であると信じていました。
dialogue.local: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.
dialogue.en: Michelangelo believed that he was a tool of God.

dialogue.text: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.
dialogue.zh: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.
dialogue.ja: 彼は大理石から彫刻を作っているのではなく、その中に閉じ込められた形を解放しているだけでした。
dialogue.local: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.
dialogue.en: He wasn't creating the sculpture from marble, he was simply releasing the figure imprisoned within it.

dialogue.text: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.
dialogue.zh: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロの未完成の作品は、彼の技術について多くの洞察を与えてくれます。
dialogue.local: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.
dialogue.en: Unfinished work by Michelangelo gives us many insights into his techniques.

dialogue.text: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.
dialogue.zh: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.
dialogue.ja: ほとんどの彫刻家は粘土のモデルを作り、その後大理石の塊に刻む場所を印をつけます。
dialogue.local: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.
dialogue.en: Most sculptors would create a clay model and then mark up their block of marble to nowhere to chip.

dialogue.text: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.
dialogue.zh: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.
dialogue.ja: しかしミケランジェロは主にフリーハンドで作業し、前から後ろへと進めました。
dialogue.local: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.
dialogue.en: But Michelangelo worked mostly freehand, starting from the front and working back.

dialogue.text: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.
dialogue.zh: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.
dialogue.ja: 大理石を彫るには、アスリートの力と外科医の器用さが必要です。
dialogue.local: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.
dialogue.en: To sculpt him marble, you need the strength of an athlete and the dexterity of a surgeon.

dialogue.text: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.
dialogue.zh: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.
dialogue.ja: どんなミスも何年もの努力を台無しにする可能性があります。
dialogue.local: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.
dialogue.en: Any slip-up can destroy years of work.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロは「ラフアウト」と呼ばれる作業から始めました、
dialogue.local: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,
dialogue.en: Michelangelo would start by what is called roughing out,

dialogue.text: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.
dialogue.zh: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.
dialogue.ja: ポイントチゼルと大きな木槌を使って大部分の石を取り除き、彫刻の大まかな形にします。
dialogue.local: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.
dialogue.en: taking the bulk of the weight off with a point chisel and a large mallet for getting it down to the general shape of the sculpture.

dialogue.text: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.
dialogue.zh: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.
dialogue.ja: 次に、歯のついたチゼルと小さなハンマーを使って、形の詳細なモデリングを行います。
dialogue.local: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.
dialogue.en: Then he would use a tooth chisel and a smaller hammer for more detailed work in modeling the form.

dialogue.text: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.
dialogue.zh: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.
dialogue.ja: より細かいディテールが必要になると、より細かい歯のついたチゼルを使いました。
dialogue.local: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.
dialogue.en: As he needed more details, he would use finer and finer tooth chisels.

dialogue.text: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.
dialogue.zh: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.
dialogue.ja: 彼はより深い隙間に入るためにドリルを使いました。
dialogue.local: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.
dialogue.en: He would use a drill to get into the deeper crevices.

dialogue.text: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.
dialogue.zh: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.
dialogue.ja: その後、様々な小さな道具を使って仕上げを行い、ラスプのようなやすりで表面を整えました。
dialogue.local: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.
dialogue.en: Then he would refine, using various smaller tools, followed by finishing the surface with a tool like the rasp, a sort of file.

dialogue.text: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.
dialogue.zh: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.
dialogue.ja: 最後に、研磨性のある軽石と革を使って彫像を磨き、滑らかで光沢のある仕上がりにしました。
dialogue.local: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.
dialogue.en: Finally, he would polish the statue using abrasive pumice stones and then leather until it is smooth and glossy.

dialogue.text: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.
dialogue.zh: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.
dialogue.ja: ここにある彼の未完成の作品を見ると、彫刻が石から浮かび上がってくるのがはっきりとわかります。
dialogue.local: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.
dialogue.en: If we look at his unfinished work here, we can clearly see the sculpture emerging from the stone.

dialogue.text: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.
dialogue.zh: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.
dialogue.ja: ここに見える跡はミケランジェロ自身の手によるものです。
dialogue.local: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.
dialogue.en: The marks we see here were made by Michelangelo's own hands.

dialogue.text: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.
dialogue.zh: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.
dialogue.ja: 外側の部分は、ミケランジェロが大きなピックと木槌で石を切り始めた場所を示しています。
dialogue.local: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.
dialogue.en: The outer part show us where Michelangelo started to cut away the stone with a large pick and a mallet.

dialogue.text: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.
dialogue.zh: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.
dialogue.ja: そしてこの部分では、彼が歯のついたチゼルを使ったのがはっきり見えます。
dialogue.local: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.
dialogue.en: And in this area, we can clearly see he has used a tooth chisel.

dialogue.text: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.
dialogue.zh: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.
dialogue.ja: 胸の部分では、さらに細かいディテールと、より細かい道具を使った跡が見られます。
dialogue.local: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.
dialogue.en: Here on the chest, we see even more detail and the marks of fainter where he has used much finer tools.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロは26歳の時に、聖書の英雄ダビデの巨大な像を彫るよう依頼されました。
dialogue.local: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.
dialogue.en: Michelangelo was 26 when he was asked to sculpt a colossal statue of the biblical hero David.

dialogue.text: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.
dialogue.zh: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.
dialogue.ja: 大聖堂の屋根に設置される予定で、地上80メートルの高さです。
dialogue.local: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.
dialogue.en: To be placed on the roof of the cathedral influence, 80 metres above street level.

dialogue.text: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.
dialogue.zh: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.
dialogue.ja: わずか2年前に彼はローマで痛ましいほど美しいピエタを彫刻し、すでに名匠と見なされていました。
dialogue.local: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.
dialogue.en: Only two years before, he had carved the achingly beautiful pierter in Rome and he was already considered a master.

dialogue.text: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.
dialogue.zh: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.
dialogue.ja: 彼は大聖堂が所有していて50年間放置されていた古い大理石の塊を使うように頼まれました。
dialogue.local: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.
dialogue.en: He was asked to use an old block of marble already owned by the cathedral that had been sitting around for 50 years.

dialogue.text: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.
dialogue.zh: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.
dialogue.ja: 他の二人の彫刻家も使おうとしましたが、大理石に欠陥があり、成功する像を作るには狭すぎると考えられていました。
dialogue.local: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.
dialogue.en: Two other sculptors had attempted to use it, but the marble was flawed and considered too narrow to produce a successful figure.

dialogue.text: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.
dialogue.zh: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.
dialogue.ja: ある彫刻家は、像の脚の間に大きな穴を彫ってしまいました。
dialogue.local: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.
dialogue.en: One sculptor had even carved a large hole out between what were to have been the legs of his figure.

dialogue.text: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.
dialogue.zh: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.
dialogue.ja: しかし他の人が欠陥と見たところを、ミケランジェロはチャンスと見ました。
dialogue.local: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.
dialogue.en: But where other saw floors, Michelangelo saw opportunity.

dialogue.text: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.
dialogue.zh: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.
dialogue.ja: 大理石の形状のために、ミケランジェロは正確でなければなりませんでした。
dialogue.local: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.
dialogue.en: Because of the shape of the marble, Michelangelo had to be precise.

dialogue.text: There was no room for manoeuvre.
dialogue.zh: There was no room for manoeuvre.
dialogue.ja: 操作の余地はありませんでした。
dialogue.local: There was no room for manoeuvre.
dialogue.en: There was no room for manoeuvre.

dialogue.text: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.
dialogue.zh: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.
dialogue.ja: 大理石が十分でなかったため、ダビデは横を向かなければなりませんでした。
dialogue.local: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.
dialogue.en: David had to look to the side as there wasn't enough marble to have him facing forward.

dialogue.text: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.
dialogue.zh: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.
dialogue.ja: ダビデはコントラポストの姿勢をとらなければならず、脚が大理石の大きな穴の周りに収まるようにしました。
dialogue.local: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.
dialogue.en: David had to be in the contra-posto position so that his legs would fit around the large hole already in the marble.

dialogue.text: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.
dialogue.zh: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.
dialogue.ja: また、大理石の深さのために、彼は細身でなければなりませんでした。
dialogue.local: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.
dialogue.en: And he would have to be slender because of the depth of the marble.

dialogue.text: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,
dialogue.zh: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,
dialogue.ja: ダビデとゴリアテの物語は、少年イスラエル人がペリシテの巨人を倒す聖書の話です、
dialogue.local: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,
dialogue.en: The story of David and Goliath is the biblical story of the Philistine giant defeated by the teenage Israelite,

dialogue.text: and only with his sling.
dialogue.zh: and only with his sling.
dialogue.ja: そして彼のスリングショットだけで。
dialogue.local: and only with his sling.
dialogue.en: and only with his sling.

dialogue.text: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.
dialogue.zh: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.
dialogue.ja: 物語の最後は、ダビデが彼の頭を切り落とし、歓声を上げる群衆にそれを掲げる場面です。
dialogue.local: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.
dialogue.en: The finale of the story is David cutting off his head and holding it up to the cheering crowd.

dialogue.text: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.
dialogue.zh: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.
dialogue.ja: 伝統的にダビデは、死んだゴリアテに勝利した瞬間に描かれてきました。
dialogue.local: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.
dialogue.en: Traditionally David had been portrayed at the point of victory triumphant over the dead Goliath.

dialogue.text: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.
dialogue.zh: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.
dialogue.ja: ドナテッロやヴェロッキオのようなフィレンツェの芸術家たちは、ゴリアテの切断された頭の上に立つダビデの自分たちのバージョンを描きました。
dialogue.local: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.
dialogue.en: Florentine artists like Donatello and Verocchio depicted their own version of David standing over Goliath's severed head.

dialogue.text: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.
dialogue.zh: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.
dialogue.ja: すべての彫像は単なる表現以上のものですが、ミケランジェロの解釈は革命的でした。
dialogue.local: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.
dialogue.en: All statues are more than mere representations, but Michelangelo's take on it would be revolutionary.

dialogue.text: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,
dialogue.zh: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,
dialogue.ja: 聖書の英雄の従来の属性を取り除き、文字通りにも比喩的にも彼を剥ぎ取ることで、
dialogue.local: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,
dialogue.en: By removing the conventional attributes of the biblical hero, stripping him down both literally and figuratively,

dialogue.text: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロはそれを単なる物語の挿絵としての単純な読み方も取り除きます、
dialogue.local: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,
dialogue.en: Michelangelo also removes a simplistic reading of it as just an illustration of the story,

dialogue.text: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.
dialogue.zh: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.
dialogue.ja: そしてそれにより、より広い比喩的な意味を与えています。
dialogue.local: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.
dialogue.en: and gives it a wider metaphorical meaning.

dialogue.text: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.
dialogue.zh: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.
dialogue.ja: 芸術史上初めて、ダビデは勝利の瞬間ではなく戦いの前に描かれています。
dialogue.local: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.
dialogue.en: For the first time in art, David is depicted before the battle rather than the moment of victory.

dialogue.text: This changes everything.
dialogue.zh: This changes everything.
dialogue.ja: これがすべてを変えました。
dialogue.local: This changes everything.
dialogue.en: This changes everything.

dialogue.text: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.
dialogue.zh: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.
dialogue.ja: 何よりもまず、ミケランジェロのダビデは理性を描いています。
dialogue.local: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.
dialogue.en: First and foremost, Michelangelo's David depicts rationality.

dialogue.text: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.
dialogue.zh: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.
dialogue.ja: ダビデはゴリアテと力任せに戦うのではなく、技術と理性で戦います。
dialogue.local: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.
dialogue.en: David isn't about to fight Goliath with brute strength, but with skill and reason.

dialogue.text: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.
dialogue.zh: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.
dialogue.ja: ダビデは、知性と意志の力だけで英雄になれる人間主義の理想を表しています。
dialogue.local: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.
dialogue.en: David represents the humanist ideal of a man who can become a hero by his intelligence and will power alone.

dialogue.text: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.
dialogue.zh: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.
dialogue.ja: これらはルネサンス時代に完璧と考えられた思考する人間の美徳です。
dialogue.local: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.
dialogue.en: These are the virtues of the thinking man considered perfection during the Renaissance.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロは、彼が目の前の挑戦を考えている集中のピークを捉えています。
dialogue.local: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.
dialogue.en: Michelangelo catches him at the peak of his concentration as he contemplates the challenge ahead of him.

dialogue.text: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.
dialogue.zh: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.
dialogue.ja: ダビデはもはや伝統的な自信に満ちた少年ではなく、不安げな男性として描かれています。
dialogue.local: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.
dialogue.en: David is no longer the traditional self-assured boy, now he is shown as an apprehensive man.

dialogue.text: David's neck is tense.

dialogue.ja: 彼らはより良い場所を探すことにし、最終的にフィレンツェの政治の中心に置くことに決めました。
dialogue.local: They decided to find a better location, and eventually decided it should be placed in the political heart of Florence.
dialogue.en: They decided to find a better location, and eventually decided it should be placed in the political heart of Florence.

dialogue.text: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.
dialogue.zh: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.
dialogue.ja: 市庁舎の前、ピアッツァ・デッラ・シニョーリアにあり、その複製は今もそこにあります。
dialogue.local: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.
dialogue.en: In Piazza della senioria, in front of the town hall, where its copy still is today.

dialogue.text: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.
dialogue.zh: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.
dialogue.ja: 委員会の一人がダビデをあまり目立たない場所に置くよう説得しようとしました。
dialogue.local: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.
dialogue.en: One member of the committee tried to persuade them to place David in a less prominent place.

dialogue.text: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.zh: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.ja: その人物はレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチです。
dialogue.local: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.
dialogue.en: His name, Leonardo da Vinci.

dialogue.text: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.
dialogue.zh: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.
dialogue.ja: ダビデは真の巨像で、高さはほぼ6メートル、重さは6トンです。
dialogue.local: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.
dialogue.en: David is truly a colossus, at nearly six metres tall and weighing six tonnes.

dialogue.text: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.
dialogue.zh: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.
dialogue.ja: 彫像をミケランジェロの工房から半マイル移動するのに、4日間と40人の男性がかかりました。
dialogue.local: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.
dialogue.en: It took four days and 40 men to move the statue half a mile from Michelangelo's workshop.

dialogue.text: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.
dialogue.zh: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.
dialogue.ja: 挑戦のジェスチャーとして、ダビデは南向きに置かれ、ローマの方を向いています。
dialogue.local: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.
dialogue.en: In a gesture of defiance David was placed facing south towards Rome.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロはその場で仕上げの手を加えました。
dialogue.local: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.
dialogue.en: Michelangelo then added the finishing touches on sight.

dialogue.text: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.
dialogue.zh: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.
dialogue.ja: 元々、スリングと切り株の支えはこれらの復元図に見られるように金で覆われていました。
dialogue.local: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.
dialogue.en: Originally the sling and tree stump support were gilded with gold as seen in these reconstructions.

dialogue.text: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.
dialogue.zh: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.
dialogue.ja: ダビデはフィレンツェ市民から熱狂的な歓迎を受け、最初から傑作であり共和国の象徴とされました。
dialogue.local: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.
dialogue.en: David received a rapturous reception from the Florentines, and right from the start it was held as a masterpiece and a symbol of the Republic.

dialogue.text: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.
dialogue.zh: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.
dialogue.ja: 16世紀のイタリアの歴史家ジョルジョ・ヴェザーリは、これを見た後は誰も他の彫刻や他の芸術家の作品を見たいとは思わないと書いています。
dialogue.local: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.
dialogue.en: The Italian 16th century historian Georgie Versari wrote, after seeing this, no one need wish to look at any other sculpture or the work of any other artist.

dialogue.text: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.
dialogue.zh: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.
dialogue.ja: 1873年、ダビデは環境被害から守るためにアカデミア美術館に移されました。
dialogue.local: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.
dialogue.en: In 1873 David was moved to the academia gallery to protect it from environmental damage.

dialogue.text: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.
dialogue.zh: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.
dialogue.ja: そして1910年に、実物大の複製が広場に置かれました。
dialogue.local: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.
dialogue.en: And in 1910 a full-sized copy was placed in the square.

dialogue.text: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.
dialogue.zh: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.
dialogue.ja: 無花果の葉は最終的に取り除かれ、ダビデはミケランジェロの意図した通りに見ることができました。
dialogue.local: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.
dialogue.en: His fig leaf was eventually removed and David could be seen as Michelangelo intended.

dialogue.text: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.
dialogue.zh: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.
dialogue.ja: 彫像は最初の解釈を超えた力を持っています。
dialogue.local: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.
dialogue.en: Statues have power beyond their initial reading.

dialogue.text: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.
dialogue.zh: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.
dialogue.ja: ある人の英雄は別の人にとっては抑圧の象徴です。
dialogue.local: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.
dialogue.en: One man's hero is another man's symbol of oppression.

dialogue.text: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence
dialogue.zh: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence
dialogue.ja: ミケランジェロは多くの傑作を生み出しましたが、彼が牧羊少年をフィレンツェの具現化に奇跡的に変えたことは
dialogue.local: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence
dialogue.en: Michelangelo would go on to create many masterpieces, but his miraculous transformation of a shepherd boy into the physical embodiment of Florence

dialogue.text: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.
dialogue.zh: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.
dialogue.ja: 彼の芸術的なキャリアの決定的な瞬間となりました。
dialogue.local: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.
dialogue.en: would prove to be a defining moment in his artistic career.

dialogue.text: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.
dialogue.zh: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.
dialogue.ja: 彼は大理石を肉体と骨に変え、これまでにない心理的洞察と物理的リアリズムを彫刻にもたらした錬金術師でした。
dialogue.local: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.
dialogue.en: He was an alchemist who turned marble into flesh and bone and brought a psychological insight and physical realism to sculpture never seen before.

dialogue.text: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.
dialogue.zh: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.
dialogue.ja: 彼は1564年2月にローマで亡くなり、88歳の時もまだ働いていました。
dialogue.local: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.
dialogue.en: He died in Rome in February of 1564, still working at the age of 88 years old.

dialogue.text: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.
dialogue.zh: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.
dialogue.ja: 彼は芸術のライバルであるレオナルド・ダ・ヴィンチとラファエロの両方よりも長生きしました。
dialogue.local: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.
dialogue.en: Having outlived both his art rivals Leonardo da Vinci and Rafael.

dialogue.text: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
dialogue.zh: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
dialogue.ja: 彼はフィレンツェに戻され、彼の神聖なダビデ像からすぐ近くのサンタ・クローチェ教会に埋葬されました。
dialogue.local: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
dialogue.en: He was brought back to Florence to be buried in Santa Crocé Church, just a stone's throw away from his divine David.
